title: PRD: Model Catalog Ingress — progressive verification, soft-pin exemptions, and runtime compatibility signaling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: We intake a rising volume of community-submitted open model weights and variants. Current gating is binary (accept/reject or full pin) and forces either immediate pinning or full trust. This creates operational and safety risks: costly rollbacks, sudden regressions in serving behavior, and unclear expectations for customers using unpinned variants. Goal: Define a progressive verification flow (lightweight runtime probes through staged verification) and a 'soft-pin exemption' mechanism that allows short-term unpinned serving with explicit compatibility signals and automated fallback triggers. The PRD defines verification levels, required metadata and runtime probes, the soft-pin exemption contract and duration, acceptance criteria for automated promotion to pinned status, and rollback/fallback policies. Scope: Applies to new third-party open-model submissions and new variants of existing community models. Excludes internal Redwood-built models and enterprise-only private model uploads. Out of scope for this ticket: UI polish of the catalog entry page (handled in a follow-up design ticket) and long-term model deprecation schedules.
acceptance_criteria: Define verification levels L0..L3 with clear pass/fail signals and required metadata for each level: L0 (ingest metadata + checksum), L1 (lightweight runtime probe: inference smoke test + shape check), L2 (compatibility probe: KV/cache sanity + perf profile), L3 (security & license review + eval suite results)

Specify a soft-pin exemption policy that allows serving unpinned community variants for up to 30 days with explicit compatibility tokens and an automated monitoring guardrail (quality/regression and cost thresholds)
Create a runtime probe spec (list of probes, execution cadence, success thresholds) that engineering can implement in ingestion pipelines and in the catalog ingestion CI
Document metadata schema required in catalog entry: runtime_compat_tags, recommended_quantization_profiles, minimal_tokenizer_spec, fallback_variant_id, provenance_url

Define automation rules: if runtime probes fail or quality regressions exceed threshold X within Y requests, automatically route traffic to pinned fallback and mark variant as suspended with audit log entry
Define promotion criteria from soft-pin to pinned: passing L3 security review, 7-day stability window with <0.5% regression rate on evaluation prompts, and no critical infra regressions
Include example lifecycle timeline for a new community variant from ingest -> L1 probe pass -> soft-pin -> L2/L3 -> pinned or suspended
Provide a clear rollback/fallback checklist for on-call and SRE: steps, dashboards to inspect, and standard notification template to affected customers
PRD reviewed and signed-off by: Product (Asha Patel), Security (Marta Ruiz), Runtime Eng (Devon Chen), Observability (Ravi Menon), and Design (Sofia Alvarez)
notes: 2026-02-20: Initial cross-functional kickoff. Attendees: Asha, Liam, Marta, Devon, Ravi, Sofia. Agreed on progressive verification concept and soft-pin 30d default.
2026-02-25: Security asked to verify license-check automation. Action: Security to supply mapping of acceptable OSS licenses and automated SPDX scanning regex (owner: Marta, ETA 2026-03-05).

2026-03-01: Engineering raised a concern about probe runtime cost; proposed solution: sample-based probes (1% of ingestion traffic) and on-demand full-suite runs in CI only. Devon to evaluate cost impact (ENG-33821).
2026-03-05: Design suggested adding explicit 'compatibility tokens' visible on catalog entries to communicate confidence level. Sofia to produce mockups in follow-up ticket DES-2202.

2026-03-08: Observability to provide threshold recommendations for regression detection and dashboards (owner: Ravi). Proposed thresholds: 0.5% quality regression, 8% latency P95 increase, 15% cost increase vs pinned baseline.
2026-03-12: PM draft PRD updated after eng/security feedback. Ready for formal review and sign-off meeting scheduled 2026-03-18.
comments: Liam O'Connor (2026-02-22): I'll scope the runtime probe implementation and return with an effort estimate. Initial guess: 3 sprints including CI integration.

Marta Ruiz (Security) (2026-02-26): We'll need to ensure the license/status checks are deterministic and provide blocking flags for L0->L1 progression. Also recommending KMS-backed provenance verification for any models claiming enterprise provenance.

Devon Chen (Runtime) (2026-03-02): Concern: KV-cache compatibility probe might be model-architecture dependent. Proposal: define a minimal common probe set and allow vendor-specific extended probes as opt-in.
Ravi Menon (Observability) (2026-03-06): We'll provide an alert runbook and dashboard template. Need final list of metrics from eng to make SLOs actionable.
Sofia Alvarez (Design) (2026-03-09): Mockups scheduled. Will include 'compatibility token' visual, probe status, and soft-pin expiry badge.
risks: Allowing short-term unpinned serving increases risk of regressions reaching customers; mitigation: conservative default sampling + automatic fallback rules
Probe execution costs could meaningfully increase ingestion cost; mitigation: sample-based probes and CI-only full-suite runs
Ambiguity in compatibility tags could confuse customers; mitigation: design token + explicit provenance links and documentation
